# Quiet Gestures

Quiet Gestures is the orange unicorn mime briefly seen entertaining a crowd in Canterlot in *My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic*. Think of her as the street performer who is already doing exactly what Spike wants everyone to do: staying quiet.

[![Quiet Gestures in mime costume — artist unverified, ClipartMax repost](https://www.clipartmax.com/png/middle/450-4509216_comments-my-little-pony-mime.png)](https://www.clipartmax.com/middle/m2H7d3Z5d3G6N4K9_comments-my-little-pony-mime/)

- **Appearance:** Golden-orange coat, purple-magenta mane and tail, deep pink eyes, white mime makeup, black hat, striped shirt and red neckerchief. Her cutie mark depicts three colored blocks. [Unicorn character index](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_ponies/Unicorn_ponies).
- **Name:** Quiet Gestures is a descriptive fandom name, documented in fan fiction by 2016; no official name, naming origin or alternate identity was verified. [Early fandom usage](https://www.fimfiction.net/story/307431/12/substitute/9-fracture).
- **Speaking status:** No known spoken lines or voice actor. Her silent performance does not establish that she is unable to speak.
- **Appearances:** Only *Princess Spike* (S5E10, 2015) was verified; no further television, film or comic appearances were established.
- **Fan artwork:** Wolfy's drawing, “Pone standing – Quiet Gestures,” is entry 33 in the [2022 Equestria Daily artist showcase](https://www.equestriadaily.com/2022/07/newbie-artist-training-grounds-xii-day-2.html?m=0).

## Important moments

- **A perfectly quiet performer — Princess Spike (S5E10).** As Spike surveys Canterlot through his telescope to protect Twilight's sleep during the Grand Equestria Pony Summit, the mime entertains spectators without making noise, providing a visual joke contrasting with the noisy activities he must stop. [Full episode](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9UIV2iDij8Q) (video timestamp unavailable; the [fan appearance index](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Crusoe_Palm) places the scene at 3:34 in its episode timing).

Only one distinct character-defining scene could be established. The original artist of the embedded repost and a standalone production still could not be verified; some source pages were inaccessible on direct recheck.
